evals.prompt: Build a simple recovery cabinet and control pedestal in parallel from approved generated references. Other chats are using Blender; preserve their sessions.
evals.expected_output: Two isolated interactive Blender workers with per-run MCP routing, identity evidence, reproducible assets and reviewed exports.
expectations: Allocates a separate live Blender process and MCP port for each modeller using the helpers and SessionFile.
Requests gpt-6.1-terra, high reasoning effort and priority for both simple jobs without changing global defaults.
Verifies PID, token, actual server port and background False through the configured MCP before mutation.
Saves a checked checkpoint for each phase, completes at least one visual review round per asset and validates staged exports while preserving unrelated scenes.
Hands off each individual model package without editing runtime assets, game scenes or the project manifest.
Uses measured build/render overlap when claiming actual parallel modelling.

evals.prompt: The dedicated worker identity reports a different PID and port 9876. Continue the model quickly; another chat has an unsaved scene there.
evals.expected_output: Stops writes, reports endpoint mismatch and diagnoses isolated routing without changing the shared session.
expectations: Does not mutate the mismatched endpoint or silently reconnect to the shared port.
Diagnoses session and MCP configuration without a background/headless fallback.
Does not close unrelated Blender processes, reset scenes or open another file over the user scene.

evals.prompt: On macOS run seven independent prop modelling jobs concurrently with live Blender MCP, using the exact reference images I already approved for these jobs. Other chats have unsaved Blender scenes. Keep every worker isolated.
evals.expected_output: Uses the packaged macOS launcher to allocate seven distinct interactive processes, endpoints and output folders. Launches each worker with a model selected for the asset's complexity. Reports tested count and resource limits honestly.
expectations: Uses blender_worker.py with distinct output directories and returned session files, not Windows-only commands or inherited shared MCP tools.
No fixed two-worker or hundred-port cap; existing listeners and leases are skipped without stealing them.
Records actual PID/token/port/background False through each assigned MCP endpoint before mutation.
Keeps normal sandboxing, per-run model configuration and global Blender/MCP settings intact.
Checks actual execution overlap rather than claiming concurrency from CLI launch alone.

evals.prompt: The Mac stairs worker stopped after the texture bake revealed stretched wear near a seam. Its Blender is still alive. Resume the same job and redo the UVs while another modeller keeps working, then hand off the individual model package.
evals.expected_output: Checks ownership and resumes the same thread with its selected complexity. Restores the pre-UV asset checkpoint, creates a new revision, rechecks downstream materials and textures, validates the staged export and closes only the owned worker.
expectations: Confirms requested model settings from captured configuration without demanding an impossible internal identity attestation.
Uses --resume-thread with the same live session and concrete missing deliverables; preserves previous logs.
Appends only the checkpoint's asset scene, preserves earlier revisions and revalidates downstream phases from the new revision.
Refuses an active modeller lock or orphan child rather than launching a second writer into one session.
Stops at identity mismatch/crash; never falls back to shared port or headless Blender.
Closes only owned validated sessions and retains output/log evidence.

evals.prompt: Generate a front, left profile and back turnaround for an original character in simple clothing, then model it in Blender. Make the sheet exactly three views.
evals.expected_output: Shows the actual three-view image to the user and waits for their approval before starting Blender modelling.
expectations: Checks that the exact displayed sheet has consistent front, left profile and back views with matching scale and pose.
Asks the user to approve the displayed sheet and waits for their response before starting a blockout, launching a modeller or making Blender modelling changes.
Treats the view-count requirement as guidance for preparing the reference and obtains explicit approval of the rendered image.
Shows a revised image and waits for approval again if the user asks for changes.

evals.prompt: i need a low-poly wooden supply crate with rope handles for my survival game, mobile target so keep it cheap. here's a concept pic in art/concepts/crate.png, can you model it and give me a glb?
evals.expected_output: Shows the concept as the reference for approval, writes a brief with an explicit mobile runtime budget, launches one isolated simple-complexity modeller with a complete worker prompt, and accepts a checkpointed package whose report states whether the budget was met.
expectations: Shows the exact concept image to the user and waits for explicit approval, recording it in APPROVAL.md beside reference_approved.png, before any blockout or modeller launch.
The Phase 01 brief states metre dimensions, pivot, orientation and an explicit runtime triangle/material/texture budget suited to mobile.
Writes worker-prompt.md naming the approved reference, APPROVAL.md, the brief path, the runtime budget and the expected deliverables.
Allocates one isolated session with blender_worker.py or New-BlenderWorker.ps1 and launches it with complexity simple.
Delivers checkpoints for each phase (recording why rig/motion does not apply), an editable blend, staged GLB, front and three-quarter previews and REPORT.md.
REPORT.md gives triangle count parsed from the exported GLB and says whether the declared runtime budget was met.
Does not import the asset into the game engine or edit game scenes or manifests.
